rules.name: Temporary files
rules.detail: Files apps leave in your temp folder. Anything changed in the last day is kept.

rules.name: Windows temporary files
rules.detail: System-wide temp folder. Anything changed in the last day is kept.

rules.name: Error reports
rules.detail: Reports Windows saved after app crashes.

rules.name: System error reports
rules.detail: Crash reports saved for all users.

rules.name: App crash dumps
rules.detail: Memory snapshots saved when apps crash.

rules.name: System crash dumps
rules.detail: Memory dumps from Windows crashes.

rules.name: Full memory dump
rules.detail: The single large dump file from a Windows crash.

rules.name: Prefetch files
rules.detail: Windows uses these to start apps faster. It builds them again as you use apps, so the first launches can be slightly slower.

rules.name: Thumbnail and icon caches
rules.detail: Windows rebuilds these as you browse folders.

rules.name: Internet cache
rules.detail: Old web cache and certificate downloads used by Windows components and legacy apps.

rules.name: Windows Update downloads
rules.detail: Update files that are already installed. Windows downloads them again if needed. Anything changed in the last 3 days is kept, so an update that is downloading or being prepared is never disturbed.

rules.name: Delivery Optimization cache
rules.detail: Update files cached to share with other PCs.

rules.name: Windows logs
rules.detail: Logs Windows wrote while installing updates, servicing itself and setting up (CBS, DISM, Windows Update, setup). Anything newer than a week is kept. Event logs, firewall logs and web server logs are not touched.

rules.name: Other Windows temporary data
rules.detail: Leftovers Windows Disk Cleanup lists on this PC: setup temp folders, Defender scan copies, diagnostic data and feedback archives. Anything changed in the last day is kept.

rules.name: Store app temporary files
rules.detail: Temporary and network cache folders Microsoft Store apps keep for themselves. Their settings and data are not touched.

rules.name: Old update files (component store)
rules.detail: Windows keeps files from superseded updates. This removes the ones no longer needed; installed updates can still be uninstalled. It can take several minutes, and the space freed is shown afterwards.

rules.name: Previous Windows installation
rules.detail: The Windows.old folder from your last upgrade. Removing it means you can no longer go back to the previous version.

rules.name: Hibernation file
rules.detail: Frees the space Windows reserves for hibernate by turning hibernate and Fast Startup off. Turn them back on any time with: powercfg /hibernate on

rules.name: Old driver versions
rules.detail: Windows removes older copies of drivers it no longer uses from the driver store, using Disk Cleanup. The size is shown afterwards.

rules.name: Windows upgrade and setup leftovers
rules.detail: Installation files, logs and discarded files from Windows upgrades and resets, removed by Disk Cleanup. Resetting the PC may need to download files again. The size is shown afterwards.

rules.name: Google Chrome cache
rules.detail: Cached pages and scripts from every profile. Sign-ins, history and bookmarks are not touched.

rules.name: Microsoft Edge cache
rules.detail: Cached pages and scripts from every profile. Sign-ins, history and bookmarks are not touched.

rules.name: Brave cache
rules.detail: Cached pages and scripts from every profile.

rules.name: Vivaldi cache
rules.detail: Cached pages and scripts from every profile.

rules.name: Opera and Opera GX cache
rules.detail: Cached pages and scripts.

rules.name: Firefox cache
rules.detail: Cached pages and scripts from every profile.

rules.name: Other browser and app caches
rules.detail: Cached pages and scripts kept by every other app built on Chromium (Electron, WebView2) found on this PC. Sign-ins and settings are not touched. Close the apps first; files they are using are skipped.

rules.name: Discord cache
rules.detail: Cached images and scripts. You stay signed in.

rules.name: Slack cache
rules.detail: Cached images and scripts. You stay signed in.

rules.name: Spotify cache
rules.detail: Songs saved for faster playback. Downloaded music for offline use is kept in a separate folder.

rules.name: VS Code cache
rules.detail: Cached code, extension downloads and old logs.

rules.name: Cursor cache
rules.detail: Cached code, extension downloads and old logs. Your settings, chats and workspaces are kept.

rules.name: OneDrive logs
rules.detail: Sync logs older than a week.

rules.name: Old app logs
rules.detail: Log files Claude, Zoom, Teams and Discord wrote. Anything newer than a week is kept.

rules.name: Steam web cache
rules.detail: Cached store and community pages inside Steam.

rules.name: Epic Games Launcher web cache
rules.detail: Cached store pages inside the launcher.

rules.name: DirectX shader cache
rules.detail: Compiled graphics shaders. Games rebuild them the next time they run.

rules.name: NVIDIA shader caches
rules.detail: Compiled graphics shaders. Games rebuild them the next time they run.

rules.name: AMD shader caches
rules.detail: Compiled graphics shaders. Games rebuild them the next time they run.

rules.name: Intel shader caches
rules.detail: Compiled graphics shaders. Games rebuild them the next time they run.

rules.name: Game web caches (Unreal Engine)
rules.detail: Cached store and login pages inside games and launchers built with Unreal Engine.

rules.name: Minecraft launcher cache and logs
rules.detail: Launcher web cache, installer downloads and game logs. Anything newer than a week is kept. Worlds and settings are not touched.

rules.name: Game launcher logs and caches
rules.detail: Logs and browser caches of the Riot, VALORANT, Roblox, Battle.net and EA launchers. Anything newer than a week is kept. You stay signed in.

rules.name: Graphics driver installer leftovers
rules.detail: Folders NVIDIA and AMD installers unpack on the system drive, and the download caches of the AMD software. Not needed after the driver is installed.

rules.name: npm cache
rules.detail: Downloaded packages. npm fetches them again when needed.

rules.name: Yarn cache
rules.detail: Downloaded packages. Yarn fetches them again when needed.

rules.name: pnpm store and cache
rules.detail: Packages pnpm keeps once for all projects. Projects keep working; pnpm downloads again what a new install needs.

rules.name: Poetry and uv caches
rules.detail: Downloaded Python packages. The tools fetch them again when needed.

rules.name: Scoop download cache
rules.detail: Installers Scoop downloaded for apps already installed. Scoop downloads them again if needed.

rules.name: Chocolatey download cache
rules.detail: Cached package feed responses.

rules.name: Chocolatey logs
rules.detail: Logs of past Chocolatey runs. Anything newer than a week is kept.

rules.name: pip cache
rules.detail: Downloaded Python packages and built wheels.

rules.name: NuGet web cache
rules.detail: Cached package feed responses and plugins.

rules.name: Go build cache
rules.detail: Compiled Go packages. Go rebuilds them when needed.

rules.name: NuGet package store
rules.detail: Every package your .NET projects restored. The next build downloads what it needs again, which can take a while.

rules.name: Gradle caches
rules.detail: Downloaded dependencies and build caches. The next build downloads and rebuilds them, which can take a while.

rules.name: Cargo downloads and sources
rules.detail: Downloaded Rust crates, their unpacked sources and git checkouts. Cargo fetches them again when needed, which can take a while.

rules.name: Go module cache
rules.detail: Downloaded Go modules. Go fetches them again when a build needs them.

rules.name: Maven repository
rules.detail: Dependencies Maven downloaded for your projects. The next build downloads them again, which can take a while.

rules.name: Conda package cache
rules.detail: Downloaded Conda packages. Environments keep working; Conda downloads again when needed.

rules.name: Bun and Deno caches
rules.detail: Packages and compiled code Bun and Deno downloaded. They fetch them again when a project needs them, which can take a while.

rules.name: Composer and vcpkg caches
rules.detail: PHP packages Composer downloaded and binaries vcpkg built. They are fetched or built again when a project needs them, which can take a while.

rules.name: IDE caches (JetBrains, Android Studio)
rules.detail: Indexes and caches of your IDEs. They rebuild on the next start, which can take a few minutes. Close the IDE first.

rules.name: Visual Studio caches
rules.detail: Component and designer caches Visual Studio rebuilds on start.

rules.name: Visual Studio installer package cache
rules.detail: Installation packages the Visual Studio Installer keeps for repairs and changes. Without them it downloads what it needs again, so repairs need an internet connection.

rules.name: Tool download caches (Electron, node-gyp, ffmpeg)
rules.detail: Binaries downloaded by build tools. They are fetched again when a project needs them.

rules.name: Test browsers (Playwright, Cypress, Puppeteer)
rules.detail: Browsers downloaded for automated tests. Tools download them again when a project needs them.

rules.name: Downloaded AI models and tool caches
rules.detail: Models and data libraries such as Hugging Face and PyTorch downloaded into your home folder. They can be large and take a long time to download again.

rules.name: Other tool caches in your home folder
rules.detail: Folders named cache inside the hidden tool folders of your user profile (for example .openjfx and .codex). The tools create them again.

rules.name: Old installers
rules.detail: Setup files in Downloads that have not changed for 60 days, even if you still run them from there. Held for 14 days so you can undo.

rules.name: Unfinished downloads
rules.detail: Partial downloads older than a week. Held for 14 days so you can undo.

rules.name: Recycle Bin
rules.detail: Files you deleted. Emptying it cannot be undone.
